observations.content: Production runs 12x m5.2xlarge on-demand in us-east-1, average CPU utilization 35%
Dev/staging runs 6x m5.xlarge on-demand 24/7, used only during business hours
ECS Fargate cluster running 8 services, average task count 24, task CPU reservation 50% but actual usage ~20%
No autoscaling policies configured; fixed task count since initial deployment
47 Lambda functions, 12 allocated at 1024MB but p99 memory usage under 256MB
Lambda costs are $1,200/month, 60% from 3 functions running on 5-minute cron schedules
Primary RDS: db.r5.2xlarge Multi-AZ PostgreSQL, $1,800/month. CPU averages 15%, storage 2TB with 500GB used
Read replica running same instance class, receives <5% of queries
18TB across 4 buckets. 14TB is log data older than 90 days in S3 Standard
S3 costs $420/month; lifecycle policies exist but only for one bucket
Data transfer costs $3,200/month, 70% is cross-AZ traffic between ECS tasks and RDS
CloudFront distribution serves static assets but origin fetches are 40% of requests due to low TTL
NAT Gateway processing 2TB/month at $0.045/GB, mostly outbound API calls from Lambda
Purchased 1-year standard RIs for c5.xlarge in 2025-Q1, but migrated to m5 family in 2025-Q3 — RIs wasted for 6 months
Attempted Spot Instances for production ECS in 2025-Q2, experienced 3 capacity reclamations in one week causing 15-minute outages each
Post-mortem: no fallback to on-demand was configured, no capacity diversification across instance types

Total monthly AWS spend: $28,400. Breakdown: EC2 $9,600, RDS $3,800, Data Transfer $3,200, ECS Fargate $3,100, S3 $420, Lambda $1,200, ElastiCache $1,400, NAT Gateway $1,080, CloudFront $600, Other $5,000
30% reduction target = $8,520 savings needed, bringing bill to ~$19,880
